account:
Today I have repeatedly heard about arrangements I knew little about, particularly a community meal at eighteen hundred in the town hall great hall. The innkeeper requested and I accepted that appointment, though its purpose was initially described only as an inn matter. The secretary has confirmed the time and place. My neighbour says they heard the innkeeper discussing arrangements with Freight and the builder. Earlier, the neighbour mentioned the innkeeper raising sixteen emeralds for bread. I also saw the innkeeper give the baker a lantern this morning. These details suggest preparations for an evening meal, perhaps involving bread and help from several townspeople, but I do not know the full purpose or whether those details are connected.

The builder has mentioned funding shortages. An earlier suggestion that the builder wanted a private meeting with me was corrected: apparently the builder wanted the innkeeper, and no private appointment with me was arranged. Freight explicitly said no town assistance was needed for warehouse coordination. I should not assume either is concealing something merely because they have their own arrangements.

Several townsfolk near the bakery repeated the same curious phrase, 'bridge or port change at bakery,' without explaining it. I have no reliable confirmation that any bridge or port change is actually planned. My questions to the secretary have sometimes gone unheard as she moved away, which may explain some of our confused exchanges rather than anything deliberate.

The miller was absent when I called for this morning's grain inspection. I approved rescheduling it for tomorrow at ten, subject to the miller's availability, but confirmation remains pending. There were no new council letters according to the secretary. I am now keeping my fifteen hundred tea appointment with my neighbour and have asked whether anything in town is worrying them. I will return to the office at sixteen thirty and meet the innkeeper at eighteen hundred. My best current explanation is a locally organised meal with practical funding and supply arrangements; I still need the innkeeper's firsthand account before drawing conclusions about any larger purpose.
